The standard draft supplies ALL, ANY, MAJORITY, MIN_SCORE, MAX_SCORE, AVERAGE,
WEIGHTED_AVERAGE, WORST_SEVERITY. Its operation requirement is openverify.aggregate, exact version 1.
Every invocation MUST provide reducer and handling. handling is a mapping
with keys UNKNOWN, ERROR, SKIP, DEFERRED, CANCELLED, NOT_APPLICABLE, MISSING.
Every key MUST have REJECT or IGNORE. No hidden default is permitted.
REJECT makes the reference aggregator raise AGGREGATE_INPUT (the engine records
an ERROR). IGNORE excludes that input. Neither invents a satisfaction value.
Known logical inputs require verdict; numeric inputs require score; severity
inputs require severity. Absent required value uses MISSING handling.
A KNOWN result with no binary verdict is not UNKNOWN.
Empty input, including empty after filtering, MUST be rejected.
ALL passes iff all retained verdicts PASS. ANY passes iff at least one PASS.
MAJORITY passes iff PASS count exceeds FAIL count, fails iff FAIL exceeds PASS.
A tie is rejected: tie resolution is not specified.
Numeric reducers produce KNOWN score without implying verdict. MIN/MAX select
extrema; AVERAGE is arithmetic mean. WEIGHTED_AVERAGE requires one finite
nonnegative weight per original input and positive retained weight total;
filtering preserves original positions. Zero total MUST be rejected.
The direct ordered-sequence API uses positional weights. Graph reducers use
explicit ordered aggregate_inputs and identity-keyed weights as specified in
[dataflow](dataflow.md). ALL standard reducers and custom Aggregate use that same
structural membership, including ERROR and nonexecuted Result members. Execution
predecessors do not determine membership; Derive/Control bookkeeping is excluded.
WORST_SEVERITY requires an explicit severity_domain {id, levels}, whose labels
are unique, nonempty and have distinct integer ranks; higher rank is worse.
Ranks follow JSON Schema integer semantics: integral JSON numbers such as 1 and
1.0 are valid; booleans, numeric strings, and fractional numbers are not ranks.
Inputs MUST refer to that domain and labels in it. Output contains its greatest
ranked severity without implying verdict. All output Results are successful,
applicable, KNOWN; evidence from retained inputs is concatenated in input order.
Verification observes, derives information, judges criteria, and controls
verification execution. It does not own arbitrary external business side effects.
Meaning, Knowledge, Computation, Composition, Execution Policy, Resources,
Result/Decision, and Provenance are inside the boundary.
Application actions, runtime implementation, external storage mechanism, model
implementation, and human workflow implementation are outside it.
The boundary argument is by question: what is to be established (Meaning);
what information exists (Knowledge); what operation is performed (Computation);
how operations relate in time (Composition); what event makes one eligible
(Activation); which subjects are included (Selection); should an eligible check
run now (Admission); what is required/consumed (Resources); what happened
(Result/Decision); how it relates across time (Provenance).
If a legitimate concern inside this declared boundary cannot be represented by
one of these questions, the model is incomplete. This is a falsifiable category
argument, not proof of complete wire syntax or implemented capabilities.
The supported executable graph is acyclic, with unique node IDs, unique directed
execution edges, and existing endpoints. Every incoming edge requires its predecessor
to reach a terminal occurrence state. Edges transfer no data and do not implicitly
propagate predecessor failure/nonexecution. Data unavailability propagates only
through explicit bindings; guards explicitly constrain eligibility.
Bindings to upstream ports require a strict execution ancestor. Node array order
is not data identity. Independent nodes may execute in any topologically valid order;
the reference executor uses definition order among ready nodes.
Equality guards, port identity, availability and aggregate membership follow
[typed dataflow](dataflow.md). Every node gets a record, including disabled/blocked
nodes. [Lifecycle](lifecycle.md) specifies exact reasons and dispositions for
admission, routing, guards, control termination, cancellation and input blocking.
ROUTE names a direct outgoing successor, excludes other exclusive branches and
preserves shared joins. It never bypasses dependencies or guards. No overall verdict
is synthesized without Aggregate. Control decisions are verification control, never
external business actions.
Cycles/iteration and DYNAMIC_EXPANSION features MUST yield GRAPH_UNSUPPORTED.
Derive produces INFORMATION, Evaluate produces a Result, and Control produces a
Decision. Aggregate is specialized Evaluate. Every kind has explicit typed inputs,
outputs, bindings and an exact provider-neutral operation requirement as specified
in [typed dataflow](dataflow.md). Information outputs may accompany Results or
Decisions; execution observations and usage remain separate from semantic outputs.
The exact input object contains only resolved declared ports. There is no injected
Context or predecessor-Results argument. Trusted local implementations are explicitly
registered; operation requirements never authorize imports or expressions.
Conformance applies to the documented wire/semantic subset, not all conceivable
verification capabilities. A parser MUST structurally validate against the shipped
schema and then enforce semantic invariants. Unsupported engine features MUST
fail clearly rather than acquire invented behavior.
conformance/manifest.json enumerates deterministic fixtures with id, description,
object_type, input, valid, expected error_code when invalid, and spec reference.

Future implementations can run this suite without executing Python.

A definition declares `run_inputs` (InputPort sequence). Names are unique.
Occurrence creation MUST reject undeclared supplied names, missing required
values, and values violating their schemas, before invoking any implementation.
Run declarations use BLOCK for required inputs and OMIT or DEFAULT for optional
ones. DEFAULT contains an explicit Constant, including a possible JSON null.
JSON Schema `default` annotations never insert values.
A node declares `operation`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `bindings`, `config`, and
optionally `config_schema`. InputPort contains name, schema, required, and
on_unavailable: BLOCK (required), OMIT (optional), or DEFAULT (optional, with
explicit default Constant). OutputPort contains name, schema, and role:
INFORMATION, RESULT, or DECISION. Names are unique within each port sequence.
Bindings are a mapping from input name to exactly one ValueSource. Required
inputs MUST be bound. Unknown target names are invalid.
ValueSource is exactly one of these disjoint strict objects:
* CONSTANT: `{kind: "CONSTANT", value: <JSON>}`.
* RUN_INPUT: `{kind: "RUN_INPUT", name: <declared run input>}`.
* EXTERNAL_REFERENCE: `{kind: "EXTERNAL_REFERENCE", reference: <ArtifactRef>}`.
* UPSTREAM_OUTPUT: `{kind: "UPSTREAM_OUTPUT", node_id, output}`.
External bindings pass the exact ArtifactRef value, never fetched bytes. Fetching,
secrets, environment, clocks, randomness, network and databases belong to explicit
run/external inputs when they affect meaning. VCP does not supply a resolver.
Configuration is definition-authored implementation behavior; semantic information
consumed by an operation belongs in ports. Config MUST NOT override bound inputs.
If declared, config_schema MUST validate config before execution.
Execution dependency != data binding. Edges constrain ordering/eligibility and
transfer no data. Each upstream binding MUST name an existing output of a strict
ancestor through execution edges. A missing ordering path, self/forward dependency
or cycle is invalid. Array position is not execution order: later-listed producers
are legal if graph dependencies put them first. Cycles/iteration and dynamic
expansion remain unsupported. Future scoped occurrences can instantiate this same
node model; no iteration scope or expansion source is defined now.
operation is `{capability_id, capability_version}`. IDs follow the Provider
Contract namespace syntax; version is an exact nonempty opaque string, with no
range/fallback semantics. This is a requirement, never provider identity. A later
runner matches the pair to a manifest and validates assembled input/config/output
against capability schemas. No discovery, selection policy, or Relay is introduced.
The local registry binds that exact pair to trusted host code. The standard reducer
capability is `openverify.aggregate`, version `1`.
An explicit concrete provider binding supplied by the host is occurrence information;
see [provider binding](provider-binding.md). The reference engine enforces that
binding and its Provider Contract schemas when the host supplies provider bindings.
For direct Provider Contract binding, capability input is the exact port-name
object, config is the exact declared node config, and COMPLETED output is the
output-port-name object. A capability specification MUST declare these shapes and
VCP interchange when applicable. Contract usage/evidence observations populate the
separate VCP execution observation channel; COMPLETED alone does not imply a valid
VCP output or a verification PASS. No implicit primitive-to-port mapping exists.
DERIVE outputs have INFORMATION role. EVALUATE/AGGREGATE MUST declare exactly one
RESULT output named `result`; CONTROL exactly one DECISION output named `decision`.
These kinds MAY additionally declare INFORMATION outputs. Result and Decision
values MUST satisfy VCP semantics as well as the port schema. Bookkeeping Results
for failed/nonexecuted Derive/Control are not declared outputs. Evaluate/Aggregate
result ports expose recorded ERROR/nonexecuted Results too, for explicit inspection.
If a node refines its Result-port schema to exclude one of those states, the
bookkeeping Result remains recorded but that port is INVALID for downstream use.
Error bookkeeping MUST NOT bypass the producer's declared port schema.
Information outputs publish atomically only on semantic success. Missing declared
outputs or extra outputs invalidate the attempt; no partial information leaks.
Produced information is not forced into Result.output.
Every EVALUATE and AGGREGATE MUST bind required `subject` and `criterion` input
ports to CONSTANT snapshots equal to the definition's subject and criterion.
The provider receives these exact semantic values in its input object. Capability
implementations MUST evaluate that subject/criterion; configuration cannot choose
an unrelated criterion. This establishes auditable meaning, not proof that an
untrusted implementation tells the truth. Aggregate membership excludes these two
semantic inputs. Emitted judgments MUST validate against judgment_schema, including
an explicitly emitted null judgment. Absent judgment differs from null.
All port/config/judgment schemas MUST be valid self-contained Draft 2020-12 object
or boolean schemas. References use resolvable local JSON Pointer fragments only;
nested resource IDs, anchors/dynamic references and external schema references are
rejected up front as SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED. Annotation payloads are not schemas.
`format` is annotation-only. Schema equality MUST distinguish booleans/numbers,
including const, enum, uniqueItems. Runtime validation is mandatory at every input
and output. Static validation MUST validate constants/defaults/references and reject
disjoint explicit primitive type sets (integer overlaps number), false schemas,
and incompatible finite const/enum sets. Other subsumption is deliberately deferred
to runtime; accepting structure does not claim general schema implication.
For each node the runtime resolves bindings without ambient state. Resolution
records AVAILABLE, ABSENT (optional unbound/omitted run input),
PRODUCER_NOT_EXECUTED, PRODUCER_ERROR, OUTPUT_MISSING, or INVALID. A valid
Evaluate ERROR Result itself is AVAILABLE; its absent information is not.
Invalid output snapshots remain observations, never usable information.
AVAILABLE values are validated against target schemas. Optional OMIT explicitly
omits unavailable/invalid inputs; DEFAULT explicitly substitutes its validated
constant. Required BLOCK inputs cause SKIPPED with reason INPUT_UNAVAILABLE;
they never produce FAIL or UNKNOWN. No stale value, null, name-based lookup, or
unrelated producer is a fallback. Every declared input has a resolution snapshot,
even when execution is disabled. Nonexecution because of guards/control/admission
is distinguished from blocked input by the node record's reason.
Guards are equality over `{source: ValueSource, pointer: JSON Pointer, value: JSON}`.
Empty pointer compares the complete value. Upstream sources MUST be ancestors of
the consumer. Sources and statically known operands MUST be validated. Invalid
pointers/known operand types are rejected; unresolved runtime optional fields make
the guard false. No expressions or global Context lookup exist. Guards observe
declared result/decision ports, typed information, run inputs, constants or refs.
All Aggregate nodes declare `aggregate_inputs`, an ordered, unique list of input
port names. Each MUST bind an upstream RESULT-role output. The list is the complete
structural reducer membership, for standard and custom reducers, independent of
edge order and predecessor states/kinds. No undeclared RESULT binding may be omitted
from membership. Members are required BLOCK inputs. Nonexecution/ERROR Results stay
members and standard handling applies; unavailable values block the aggregate.
Weights in graph WEIGHTED_AVERAGE are an exact name-to-nonnegative-number mapping
over aggregate_inputs, with positive total. Filtering preserves identities. The
direct reducer SDK's ordered sequence API retains aligned positional weights.
Evidence concatenation follows aggregate_inputs order for all standard reducers.
Every Aggregate also MUST declare required `members` input bound to a CONSTANT
equal to aggregate_inputs. This supplies the authored ordering in the exact input
object received by custom implementations; JSON object member order is irrelevant.
The reserved semantic names subject, criterion and members cannot be member names.
Execution policies that consume information MUST use the same typed declarations
and ValueSource bindings (run/constants/external only, before graph execution).
The reference engine implements MANUAL/EXPLICIT and ALWAYS/PROBABILITY shorthands
and registered custom operations with role-constrained outcomes; see
[execution policy](execution-policy.md). It validates the complete definition
before invoking any policy or node.
Context now means optional ambient NONSEMANTIC host metadata. It is retained as
initial_context in provenance, never passed as computation input or mutated by
Derive. Engine.run's supplied values are run_inputs, not Context. Each invocation
receives a fresh exact input object and separate config. An implementation using
ambient information to change portable meaning violates the capability contract.
ExecutionObservation is the standard local/wire semantic observation channel:
`outputs`, `usage`, `evidence`, optional `error` {code,message}. It is not a Provider
Contract Outcome. All node kinds use this channel, including custom Aggregate.
Valid incurred usage/evidence MUST be retained separately from semantic output
acceptance, including invalid judgment/output and explicit execution errors.
Engine timing remains separate from executor usage; units are never merged.
An implementation that raises without reporting usage cannot have that unknown
usage reconstructed. It can report an error observation with incurred usage.
ExecutionObservation.usage is authoritative for the attempt. Result.usage, when
present, MUST agree on its dimensions with that observation and is a repeated
snapshot, never an additive charge. A mismatch invalidates semantic output without
erasing the valid execution observation.
Observation evidence is structurally typed but remains an observation until
semantic acceptance. Invalid Evidence meaning invalidates acceptance while its
observed snapshot and valid usage remain recorded, just like invalid port values.
RunRecord stores immutable occurrence run_inputs and ambient initial_context.
Each NodeRecord stores operation requirement, executor identity/version when known,
input resolutions (source, status, explicit value only when usable, used_default),
exact assembled input_values, observed outputs, accepted information outputs,
semantic Result/Decision, execution state/reason, usage/evidence and timing.
Source identity is (run_id, node_id, output); definitions identify run/constants.
Validators MUST reconstruct resolutions from definition, initial run inputs and
earlier node records; compare all snapshots with JSON type equality; validate
outputs and judgments; reject unbound input values and aggregate membership drift.
No provider rerun is required. This detects contradictions along declared edges,
not coordinated rewriting of an entire consistent record or forged provider truth.
Unadmitted/disabled/blocked nodes MUST NOT contain executor observations or usage.
Severity.domain remains an opaque profile/domain identifier unless an explicit
domain is supplied (e.g. WORST_SEVERITY config). No registry or implicit version
resolution exists; the identifier MUST identify a versioned semantic domain when
versions matter. Parsing Result does not claim its label belongs to an unresolved
domain. WORST_SEVERITY validates against its explicit domain snapshot.
Node executor_ref/global Context/prior-results injection and implicit graph reducer
membership are removed. Nodes require operation/ports/bindings; definitions require
run_inputs; RunRecord uses explicit resolutions and observations. Old records and
definitions must be reauthored. Protocol status remains DRAFT.
The order is activation, selection, admission, then graph execution. Resources
are typed estimates, constraints or observations, not another decision stage.
Policy decisions MUST NOT inspect graph execution or undeclared ambient Context.
All three roles reuse InputPort, ValueSource bindings, OperationRequirement,
config and optional config_schema from [dataflow](dataflow.md). Required ports
MUST be bound. Only CONSTANT, RUN_INPUT and EXTERNAL_REFERENCE are legal before
graph execution. External references supply ArtifactRef, never fetched content.
Defaults, omissions and runtime schema validation follow ordinary port semantics.
All definition structure, schemas, constants and bindings MUST validate before
any implementation is invoked. Required unavailable/invalid policy inputs,
implementation exceptions and invalid outcomes abort policy evaluation; they MUST
NOT invent a decision or occurrence.
A custom policy declares operation: {capability_id, capability_version}. Its
implementation receives only the exact resolved input object and separate config,
and returns the role outcome object directly. The role fixes the output schema:
* Activation: {outcome: ACTIVATE | DO_NOT_ACTIVATE, reason: nonempty string}.
* Selection: {subjects: ArtifactRef[], reason: nonempty string}. Subjects form a
set identified by id; duplicate identities are invalid.
* Admission: {outcome: RUN | SKIP | DEFER, reason: nonempty string}.
A Result, Decision, observation envelope or arbitrary boolean is not a policy
outcome. Candidate facts/identities needed by selection MUST be bound inputs.
This draft defines one subject per definition: selection MUST return either an
empty set or the exact definition subject snapshot. Other subjects require other
definitions/opportunities; selection does not expand or mutate graphs. General
subject-universe execution remains unsupported. A custom policy needing the
subject MUST explicitly bind it.
Legacy built-in shorthands remain: activation executor_ref MANUAL returns ACTIVATE
for a host-offered opportunity; selection executor_ref EXPLICIT returns the
structural definition subject; admission strategy ALWAYS returns RUN. PROBABILITY
requires finite p in [0,1]; p=0 SKIP, p=1 RUN, otherwise sampling returns RUN/SKIP.
A policy MUST choose exactly one of operation and its built-in discriminator
(executor_ref or strategy). Built-ins have no ports, bindings or config; only
PROBABILITY accepts probability. Other legacy names remain valid references but
unsupported locally. Custom policies cannot carry a built-in discriminator or p.
Hosts MUST provide a nonempty opportunity_id. The built-in sampler's complete
structural inputs are definition fingerprint, subject identity, opportunity_id
and explicit p. Its exact bucket identity is reference-only, not portable.
Custom policies needing opportunity identity MUST bind it as ordinary typed data.
There is no hidden budget, risk, history, clock or environment input. A budget-aware
policy simply declares the relevant typed values or external snapshots and returns
an ordinary admission outcome. Policy logic remains replaceable.
DO_NOT_ACTIVATE ends the opportunity before selection, with no occurrence.
Empty selection ends it before admission, with no occurrence for that subject.
Neither case creates a RunRecord or node records. Hosts MAY audit opportunities
outside RunRecord; no opportunity-audit object is defined here.
An occurrence is created exactly when valid admission returns RUN, SKIP or DEFER
for an activated, selected subject. RUN enables graph execution. SKIP creates one
terminal SKIPPED Result per node with ADMISSION_SKIP. DEFER creates one DEFERRED
Result per node with ADMISSION_DEFER. Neither invokes graph providers. These
states are never FAIL, ERROR or UNKNOWN. Policy failure before valid admission
creates no occurrence.
Each occurrence retains all three ordered policy evaluations: role, exact input
resolutions/values, constrained outcome and known executor identity/version.
RunRecord.admission repeats the admission outcome exactly. Validation reconstructs
policy inputs without rerunning policy logic; these are observations, not proof
of an honest implementation.
Engine.attempt returns None when no occurrence exists. Engine.run is a convenience
requiring an occurrence and raises NO_OCCURRENCE for those opportunities. Neither
fabricates records. Required unavailable/invalid policy inputs raise POLICY_INPUT;
invalid outcomes raise POLICY_OUTPUT. Custom policies use the same explicit local
exact-pair registry as graph operations; no provider selection is defined.
No periodic scheduler, policy language, multi-subject expansion or retry scheduling
is implemented. Maximum staleness/history coverage and portable sampling remain OPEN.
An extension object contains namespace, version, required (boolean), and data
(JSON value). Namespace MUST be a nonempty identifier containing a colon, such
as org.example:locator. No registry service is required.
Core fields MUST be strictly validated; unknown core fields MUST be rejected.
Core fields MUST be strictly validated; unknown core fields MUST be rejected.
Unknown optional extension data MUST be preserved without interpreting its meaning.
A consumer unable to implement a required extension MUST report
EXTENSION_UNSUPPORTED. The reference SDK/engine has no extension capability
implementations and therefore rejects all required extensions.
Metadata remains arbitrary JSON annotations and cannot override core meaning.
Context is optional ambient NONSEMANTIC host metadata: a mapping of names to JSON values. Portable information uses explicit typed inputs and bindings; see [dataflow](dataflow.md).
ArtifactRef contains id, type (media/type identifier), locator, optional schema_id,
metadata, and extensions. Its locator is an opaque structured value identifying
external content; implementations MUST NOT assume it contains artifact bytes or
automatically fetch it. Hosts supply content through declared run inputs; Derive produces declared information outputs.
Evidence contains optional id, nonempty message, artifact_ref, locator,
structured_data, metadata, and extensions. At least one of message, artifact_ref,
locator, or structured_data MUST be non-null; id and metadata alone do not count.
Empty structured mappings/sequences remain meaningful data. Empty messages do not.
Locator semantics are profile/extension-owned and opaque to core. Fundamental
Evidence properties MUST NOT encode code-specific paths or line numbers.
Only activated, selected opportunities with valid admission outcomes are
occurrences; see [execution policy](execution-policy.md). Every node has exactly
one terminal record, including nodes that never execute.
Logically a node is PENDING until all incoming prerequisites are terminal, READY
when policy/routing/guards/required inputs permit execution, RUNNING when the
runner starts an attempt, then TERMINAL. Pending/ready nodes may become terminal
without starting. This is not a new wire enum. Terminal record states are
SUCCESS, ERROR, NONEXECUTED, and CANCELLED (an interrupted attempt).
Invoked Evaluate/Aggregate implementations MUST return EXECUTED with SUCCESS or
ERROR. Returning SKIPPED/DEFERRED/CANCELLED is invalid graph output and becomes
EXECUTED/ERROR. Standalone Result interchange and direct reducers may still use
all dispositions. Successful Derive/Control retain information/Decision without
a fabricated evaluation Result. NOT_APPLICABLE means evaluation ran and found
no applicable criterion; UNKNOWN means it ran without determining an answer.
FAIL is a known judgment; exceptions/output rejection are EXECUTED/ERROR.
None of those states represents nonexecution. Nonexecuted/cancelled Results contain no evaluation fields
or successful evaluation evidence. Diagnostic output and incurred usage remain
possible. Cancelled attempts publish no accepted information or Decision.
Runner-synthesized nonexecution has stable NodeRecord.reason codes, repeated in
Result.output.reason:
| Cause | Disposition | Reason |
| Admission SKIP | SKIPPED | ADMISSION_SKIP |
| Admission DEFER | DEFERRED | ADMISSION_DEFER |
| Explicit cancellation prevents or interrupts work | CANCELLED | CANCELLATION |
| STOP_SUCCESS / STOP_FAILURE | SKIPPED | CONTROL_STOP |
| Control DEFER | DEFERRED | CONTROL_DEFER |
| Control RETRY | SKIPPED | RETRY_REQUESTED |
| Excluded route branch | SKIPPED | ROUTE_EXCLUDED |
| False/unavailable guard operand | SKIPPED | GUARD_FALSE |
| Required input unavailable/invalid | SKIPPED | INPUT_UNAVAILABLE |
CONTINUE changes no eligibility. STOP_SUCCESS/STOP_FAILURE intentionally end
further work without synthesizing a verification verdict. DEFER prevents further
work in this occurrence. RETRY ends the local pass and records its Decision;
no scheduling or new occurrence is implied.
ROUTE MUST name a direct outgoing execution successor of that Control. Exclude
other successors and their descendants except nodes also reachable from the
selected successor (shared joins). Independent work outside those branches stays
eligible. Exclusions accumulate and cannot be undone. Routing never bypasses
prerequisites/guards. All incoming guards must hold. Ordinary false guards do not
implicitly disable unguarded descendants: explicit RESULT bindings may inspect
nonexecution, while unpublished information remains unavailable.
Precedence for an unstarted node is admission non-RUN, cancellation already
observed, earlier terminating control, route exclusion, false guard, blocked input.
Occurrence DEFER/cancellation therefore never collapses into INPUT_UNAVAILABLE.
Completed terminal records never change retroactively.
Cancellation is an explicit host decision/event, distinct from failed, unknown,
skipped or deferred. RunRecord.cancellation identifies the first affected node,
phase BEFORE_START or RUNNING, and host reason. It is legal only in admission RUN.
BEFORE_START makes that and subsequent unstarted nodes NONEXECUTED/CANCELLED.
RUNNING makes the affected node state CANCELLED with a CANCELLED Result; later
nodes are NONEXECUTED/CANCELLED. Earlier terminal records remain unchanged.
Cancellation cannot be inferred from a provider Result.
The sequential engine accepts a host Cancellation token, checked before attempts
and immediately after invocation, before accepting outputs. Exceptions during a
cancelled invocation still yield CANCELLED. Cancellation after the final terminal
transition has no effect. This is cooperative and cannot preempt blocking code.
Interrupted attempt observations/usage may be retained but cannot become accepted
evaluation/information. No distributed cancellation system is defined.
Every verification requires a Subject and Criterion. Subject identifies what is
being examined; Criterion identifies the property to establish.
Selection MUST remain distinct from Criterion.
A portable VerificationDefinition MUST contain protocol marker, id, version,
subject (ArtifactRef), criterion (id and description), judgment_schema, graph,
run_inputs, and execution_policy. Optional satisfaction_mapping describes a mapping's identity
or configuration; execution remains adapter-owned. Metadata and extensions carry
additional information. Explicit id/version and a reference-only fingerprint
identify definition evolution in provenance.
Criterion metadata describes and identifies a criterion; it is not an expression
language. Evaluate adapters execute criteria. judgment_schema is a JSON Schema object or boolean describing judgments when present. A definition consumer MUST verify it
is a valid Draft 2020-12 schema. The reference engine MUST validate emitted

judgments against it. External or unresolved schema references invalidate a definition up front; schemas use the self-contained subset in [dataflow](dataflow.md). Evaluate semantic ports bind the definition subject and criterion explicitly.
[Typed dataflow](dataflow.md) defines the complete node input/output lineage contract.
RunRecord contains definition snapshot, opaque reference-only definition_fingerprint,
subject, initial supplied run_inputs, ambient nonsemantic initial_context, admission,
opportunity identity, complete node records and all final Results. It does not invent
an overall verdict. Every node has exactly one terminal record in dependency order.
Node records retain operation requirements, kind, executor identity/version when known,
exact input resolutions and values, direct upstream Result snapshots, execution
observations, accepted information and Result/Decision, resource usage and timing.
A validator reconstructs each resolution from recorded source values and checks
semantic output acceptance, availability and guard/control/admission eligibility.
No provider is rerun. Contradictions are PROVENANCE_LINEAGE errors. Usage on executor
observations remains distinct from engine wall-time usage and semantic Results.
For concrete bound providers, [provider binding](provider-binding.md) requires the
exact four-part invocation binding, matching node provenance and executor identity.
Host provider-output schema rejections preserve observations and incurred usage.
Input/output comparisons distinguish JSON booleans from numbers and preserve array
order. Admission SKIP requires all node Results SKIPPED/ADMISSION_SKIP; admission DEFER
requires DEFERRED/ADMISSION_DEFER. Disabled/blocked nodes
contain no executor observations. Every record is within its run interval and each
predecessor finishes before its consumer starts. Timestamps are UTC RFC3339 with
Z/z or +00:00. Timing establishes recorded ordering, not clock trust.
Memory and local JSONL stores are replaceable convenience implementations. The
local-sha256 fingerprint is nonportable and is not an integrity signature. Consistent
coordinated record rewriting and forged implementation behavior cannot be detected
without external trust. Edge contradictions can be detected without replay.
RunRecord.policy_evaluations contains exactly ACTIVATION, SELECTION, ADMISSION
in that order. Each PolicyEvaluation stores exact declared input values and
InputResolution snapshots, the role-constrained outcome, and optional actual
executor_ref/executor_version. Its operation requirement remains in the definition.
Activation MUST be ACTIVATE and selection MUST contain the exact definition subject;
Activation MUST be ACTIVATE and selection MUST contain the exact definition subject;
otherwise no occurrence and no RunRecord exists. The admission outcome MUST equal
RunRecord.admission. Built-in outcomes are checked against their definition;
custom policy logic is not rerun. PROBABILITY records enforce p=0/p=1 boundaries
and RUN/SKIP outcomes, but do not enforce a reference-only bucket identity.
Invalid policy provenance is PROVENANCE_LINEAGE.
NodeRecord.reason is the stable machine-readable lifecycle cause for nonexecution;
its Result repeats it in diagnostic output. [Lifecycle](lifecycle.md) defines
precedence and exact mappings. Nonexecuted records have no executor identity,
observations, accepted information, Decision or executor usage. Engine wall time
is separate bookkeeping. Interrupted cancellation is state CANCELLED and may retain
unaccepted observations/usage; RunRecord.cancellation records the first affected
node, BEFORE_START/RUNNING phase and explicit host reason. Validators reconstruct

The small public surface is `from openverify import Relay, Graph`. `Relay.run`
accepts a Graph, VerificationDefinition, or serialized VCP JSON and explicit typed
inputs. It returns `Run(record)` with `results`, `decisions`, `evidence`, `usage`,
and `to_json()`. `results` is the complete per-node final-result mapping, including
ERROR/nonexecution bookkeeping. `evidence` includes observation and Result
snapshots; repeated evidence is not an additional measurement. `usage` remains
per-node and preserves units; it is never blindly summed. `record` is an SDK
RunRecord. `RelayError`/`ProtocolError` expose stable `code`, `message`, and details.

These are narrow typing.Protocol interfaces with SDK values and small dataclasses,
defined in `relay.ports`. Hosts inject replacements into Relay's constructor. The
application revalidates driver reports; replacing physical execution does not
remove Provider Contract validation. Binder choices are independently checked
against the trusted catalog and exact manifest/capability identities.
Preparation snapshots/validates the definition, entire input contract and supplied
JSON. Binding resolves graph and policy requirements before policy execution.
Activation and selection can raise NO_OCCURRENCE without creating a record.
Admission RUN/SKIP/DEFER creates an occurrence. Built-ins MANUAL/EXPLICIT,
ALWAYS/PROBABILITY and custom provider-backed policies are supported. Probability
uses a local deterministic SHA256 bucket with definition fingerprint, subject,
opportunity identity and p. It has no portable bucket-compatibility promise.
Omitting opportunity_id generates a fresh UUID; supply one for repeatable sampling.
The state machine advances PENDING -> READY -> RUNNING -> TERMINAL, or records
explicit nonexecution. Ready non-Control nodes run in bounded waves. Whole waves
settle before successors start. Records are accepted in deterministic definition
order within each wave, irrespective of completion order. Control nodes are serial
barriers: STOP, ROUTE, RETRY and DEFER cannot race with active independent work.
All incoming prerequisites, equality guards, routing exclusions, availability,
input defaults and nonexecution precedence come from the existing SDK.
Recorded cancellation tokens serialize that occurrence, because current VCP
provenance represents one interrupted attempt. Task cancellation cleans up active
processes and raises CancelledError; it returns no fabricated completed record.
Other concurrently executing runs keep their own states and inputs. Shared Python
providers serialize by default; hosts explicitly opt into `concurrency_safe=True`.
Every invocation crosses manifest, exact capability/version, input/config schema,

outputs retain raw observations and valid incurred usage. Partial resource events
are snapshots; final usage supersedes them. Runner timing uses wall_time in seconds,
or relay_wall_time when a provider already reports wall_time in another unit.

Routes are Decisions naming a direct successor, with shared joins retained.

expansion, unsupported required extensions, and external schema references reject.

UNKNOWN, ERROR, SKIP, DEFERRED, CANCELLED, NOT_APPLICABLE, MISSING. Ignoring all
members and majority ties are errors, never automatic PASS.

policy outcomes are direct. This normalization is provider authoring, not a
runtime bypass of schemas. Ordinary externally invoked output is never wrapped.

The following table specifies v1 standard capability meaning. Manifest schemas
are available through `providers inspect`; all Evaluate/Aggregate inputs also
include explicit subject and criterion. All declared information outputs must
match graph port declarations exactly.
| Capability (`openverify.` prefix) | Inputs; configuration | Outputs/meaning |
| read_text | file | UTF-8 text and identity {path,sha256,size}; missing/binary/oversized is ERROR |
| read_file | file | base64 bytes and identity; bounded binary observation |
| select_files | directory; mode files/glob/directory, files/glob | Sorted authorized file paths |
| git_scope | cwd, base; mode WORKTREE/STAGED/UNSTAGED, include_untracked | changed_files, changed_hunks, diff, candidate, changes, deleted_files |
| candidate_unchanged | cwd, candidate | FAIL with stale_candidate if checked identities/content/HEAD changed |
| ruff | cwd, files; select diagnostic codes | Result plus findings; exit 1 is lint FAIL, runner errors are ERROR |
| pytest | cwd; optional tests (default []) | Full test scope by default; exit 1 is FAIL, exits 2–5 are ERROR |
| astgrep | cwd, files; language/pattern OR rule_file | Whole-file findings from actual CLI, normalized source coordinates |
| scope | findings, files, ranges; mode files/changed_files/directory/changed_spans/ast_ranges | Filtered findings; directory mode requires directory config |
| no_findings | findings | PASS iff supplied findings are empty |
| text | text, optional required_terms/prohibited_terms; optional required/prohibited/patterns | Deterministic literal/regex Result with structured missing/match findings |
| json_parse | text | Strict parsed value; duplicate keys/nonfinite/malformed JSON error |
| schema | value; schema | SDK offline JSON Schema property check |
| action_policy | action,target,allowed_prefixes | Only delete under an allowed directory prefix passes; rejects traversal/absolute paths |
| gate | checked Result | CONTINUE only for successful applicable known PASS; otherwise STOP_FAILURE |
| command | no inputs; host Command object fixes argv/cwd/env | observation {argv,cwd,returncode,stdout,stderr}; no automatic verdict |
| command_check | observation; exit_code, optional stdout/stderr required substrings | Verify host-supplied or captured command observations |
| aggregate | explicit members, Results and semantic inputs; reducer/handling | VCP standard reducers |
Text input terms and configured terms combine; configuration never overwrites
bound semantic inputs. Text offsets are zero-based Unicode indices, end exclusive;
lines/columns are one-based. Tool finding ranges use one-based half-open end
coordinates. Changed Git hunks use one-based new-file start/count; zero-count
deletions contain no new-file lines. AST intersection compares full half-open
ranges; changed-line filtering compares occupied lines.
The local `scope` provider accepts native paths on the running platform and
relative POSIX paths (`selected/nested/file.py`). Windows accepts both separators
and mixed separators; POSIX keeps backslashes as literal filename characters and
remains case-sensitive. Comparisons use path components with the platform's case
rules, resolving relative spellings against the process working directory.
Trailing separators do not change directory membership. `selected` includes its
children and nested descendants, but excludes `selected-other`. Exact file and
range comparisons use the same normalization. Returned findings retain their
original file strings and coordinates.
Scope filtering is lexical: it does not require paths to exist, read files, or
resolve symlinks. Deleted/missing locations can still match. An empty file list
selects nothing. An empty directory, NUL, parent traversal (`..` components), or
Windows drive-relative/root-relative or reserved path is rejected, rather than broadening
the selection. Use `.` explicitly for the current directory. FileAccess remains
responsible for authorizing actual filesystem I/O and resolving symlinks.
Zero-length ranges intersect nothing; end coordinates are exclusive.
`action_policy.allowed_prefixes` names relative directories: `tmp` and `tmp/`
both permit `tmp/item` and `tmp/nested/item`, and exclude `tmp-other/item` and
the directory `tmp` itself. Absolute targets/prefixes, empty or `.` prefixes,
ambiguous Windows paths and traversal fail closed. All supplied prefixes must
be valid. This policy compares local names, without granting filesystem access
or authenticating a later action's resolved target. It preserves supplied target
strings in denial findings. These are local standard-provider rules, not changes
to VCP or Provider Contract.
Git WORKTREE compares explicit base commit to tracked working content; STAGED
compares base to the index; UNSTAGED compares index to worktree and requires empty
base. `include_untracked` is explicit in every scope config. Untracked files get
whole-file new ranges. Renames preserve old/new paths in changes; deleted paths
are reported separately and excluded from executable file scopes. Candidate
fingerprints describe actual working content. Staged scope alone is not a claim
that tools checked index bytes: materialize a separate checkout to verify those.
The shipped code graph uses WORKTREE, base supplied by the host, and untracked files.
Ruff runs isolated with explicit codes; it does not execute repository Ruff config.
pytest executes configured tests/repository Python code and plugins with actual
process privileges. AST rules are actual ast-grep pattern rules or authorized rule
files, not a substitute parser. Tools are found in the active Python scripts
directory, then PATH, at trusted catalog construction. Hosts can pass explicit
`Tools(FileAccess(...), ruff=..., pytest=..., astgrep=...)`. Git is installed
separately. Missing tools return actionable execution ERROR messages.

Relay is a local execution harness, **not a security sandbox**. Python providers,
pytest tests/plugins and authorized external tools run with their process's real
privileges. Use separate OS accounts, containers, or equivalent host isolation for
untrusted executable code. No graph can name an executable and automatically
authorize it through the generic command capability.
The host approves provider registration, entry-point names, stdio argv/cwd/env,
filesystem roots, executable paths, timeout and concurrency. Graphs choose among
available capabilities and supply typed data/config. Caller authorization remains
the host's responsibility. A graph's config is not trusted executable config.
Only an explicitly registered Command fixes generic command argv/cwd/environment;
the default catalog provides command observation verification but no command
launcher registration. External network access requires a configured provider;
Relay performs no automatic artifact or schema fetching.
Filesystem operations resolve paths against authorized roots; default roots are
the current working directory at Relay/catalog construction. Relative document
paths require one configured root. `--root` replaces defaults and can be repeated.
Tool files must also belong to the declared cwd. Symlinks resolving outside roots
reject. These checks do not create an atomic filesystem sandbox against a hostile
process racing path changes. File reads are bounded to 2 MiB and selection to
10,000 files by default, configurable with FileAccess. Binary documents explicitly
error; read_file provides bounded base64 observation instead.
Subprocesses use argv arrays and explicit absolute cwd, with no shell=True. Default
environment inheritance is from the trusted host process; pass a complete env
mapping on Command or StdioTransport to restrict it. On Windows only SystemRoot
is supplemented when required for OS runtime services. No secrets are automatically
copied into graph ports or logs. Be aware that graph snapshots, full RunRecords,
provider diagnostics/evidence and command output may intentionally contain caller
secrets. Store/share them according to your application policy.
The local driver enforces a per-invocation host timeout (30 s default), independent
of provider-declared deadlines. It does not send an unsupported provider deadline
or claim budget enforcement. Commands bound output to 2 MiB per stream; stdio uses
the SDK's 16 MiB message limit and 1 MiB stderr limit. Violations/transport loss are
ERROR, never criterion FAIL. Provider event capture is bounded to 10,000 events
and 16 MiB by default (LocalDriver settings); deterministic text findings are
bounded to 10,000 observations. Cancellation sends a cooperative request where
supported, then terminates the process tree within a bounded grace period.
On Windows a supervisor establishes a kill-on-close Job Object **before** tool
code starts. Its descendants belong to that job even after the tool parent exits.
On POSIX a new session/process group is killed on cleanup. Programs deliberately
escaping their process group are outside this local lifetime mechanism; use OS
isolation when running hostile code. Cleanup is tested on the current platform.
No claims of cross-platform runtime testing are made merely from having both code
paths. Providers should not daemonize or retain inherited pipes after completion.
In-process providers must be async and cooperative. Sync callbacks reject at
decoration. Blocking native code or a coroutine suppressing cancellation cannot
be forcibly stopped safely inside Python; configure it as a stdio provider for a
physical termination boundary. Regex patterns run in a bounded worker process,
because stdlib regex itself cannot be preempted. Deterministic substring checks
remain local. Unknown/malformed provider events, duplicate terminal outcomes,
identity substitution, schema/type mismatches and invalid semantic outputs reject.
Git code checks associate observations with captured worktree/HEAD/content
fingerprints and perform a later freshness check. This is a best-effort stale
check, not an atomic workspace snapshot. Changes and reverts between observations
cannot be detected reliably without a host-provided immutable checkout/snapshot.
Separate worktrees avoid ordinary agent collisions. Tracked diff identities and untracked membership are rechecked too; filesystem
races and change/revert sequences still favor immutable candidates for
high-assurance checks.
Provider Binding provenance detects structural contradictions, not authenticity of
a binary, service, tool output or host. Coherently rewriting an entire record is
not detectable without an independent authenticated authority. The local-sha256
definition fingerprint is not a signature or portable canonical hash. Optional
Relay invocation annotations are not authenticated and are not independently
replayed by the VCP SDK. No stronger guarantee is advertised.
